implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Renders the navigation header showing 'Event Manager' as the logo/title, with links to 'All Events' and 'New Event'. Highlights the active nav link based on the current request path using an inline conditional CSS class.
implementation.name: application.html.erb (Header & Navigation)
implementation.pseudo_code:
RENDER HTML layout
  HEAD: title = 'Event Manager', CSRF tags, inline CSS styles
  BODY:
    HEADER with class 'header':
      LINK 'Event Manager' -> root_path (logo)
      NAV links:
        LINK 'All Events' -> events_path
          IF request.path == events_path OR root_path THEN add 'active' class
        LINK 'New Event' -> new_event_path
          IF request.path == new_event_path THEN add 'active' class
    Breadcrumbs section (see below)
    MAIN content:
      IF notice present: render green .notice paragraph
      IF alert present: render red .alert paragraph
      YIELD (page-specific content)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Renders breadcrumb navigation beneath the header. Displays clickable path segments for Home, Events, and the current page (event title or action label). Parent segments are always clickable links.
implementation.name: application.html.erb (Breadcrumbs)
implementation.pseudo_code:
RENDER breadcrumb list:
  ITEM: LINK 'Home' -> root_path (always present)
  IF request.path != root_path AND != events_path:
    ITEM: LINK 'Events' -> events_path
  IF path includes '/events/new':
    ITEM: SPAN 'New Event' (current, not a link)
  ELSE IF path matches /events/:id/edit:
    ITEM: LINK @event.title -> event_path(@event) (if @event present)
    ITEM: SPAN 'Edit' (current, not a link)
  ELSE IF path matches /events/:id (not edit):
    IF @event present:
      ITEM: SPAN @event.title (current, not a link)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Displays the list of all events sorted by newest first (ordered by controller). Each event item shows title, assigned user count badge, description (or 'No description'), and action buttons: View, Edit, Remove. Includes a confirmation dialog for removal. Shows empty-state message with link to create first event when no events exist.
implementation.name: index.html.erb (Event List)
implementation.pseudo_code:
RENDER h1 'Events'
RENDER LINK 'Add New Event' -> new_event_path

FOR EACH event IN @events:
  RENDER event-item:
    SHOW event.title
    IF event.assigned_user_count > 0:
      SHOW badge with count
    SHOW event.description OR 'No description'
    ACTIONS:
      LINK 'View' -> event_path(event)
      LINK 'Edit' -> edit_event_path(event)
      FORM DELETE event_path(event) with onsubmit confirm('Are you sure?'):
        SUBMIT 'Remove'

IF @events is empty:
  RENDER message 'No events yet.' with LINK 'Add your first event' -> new_event_path

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Renders the detailed view of an event, showing title, description (or 'No description'), and assigned user names retrieved from external service. Shows 'No users assigned' message when empty. Provides Edit, Back to Events, and Remove action buttons with confirmation for removal.
implementation.name: show.html.erb (Event Detail)
implementation.pseudo_code:
RENDER h1 @event.title
RENDER @event.description OR 'No description'

SECTION 'Assigned Users':
  assigned_users = @event.assigned_users
  IF assigned_users present:
    FOR EACH user IN assigned_users:
      RENDER badge with user avatar initial and user['name']
  ELSE:
    RENDER 'No users assigned to this event.'

ACTIONS:
  LINK 'Edit' -> edit_event_path(@event)
  LINK 'Back to Events' -> events_path
  FORM DELETE event_path(@event) with onsubmit confirm('Are you sure?'):
    SUBMIT 'Remove'

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Shared form partial used for both creating and editing events. Provides title (required) and description (optional) fields, plus a user assignment section with a search input, scrollable checkbox list showing name and email from externally loaded users, multi-select checkboxes, and a live selection counter. Also renders Cancel link back to events list.
implementation.name: _form.html.erb (Event Form)
implementation.pseudo_code:
RENDER form for event model:
  IF event has errors:
    RENDER error messages in .alert div

  FIELD: text_field :title (required)
  FIELD: text_area :description (optional)

  FIELD 'Assign Users':
    HIDDEN FIELD event[assigned_user_ids][] = '' (ensures empty array on no selection)
    user-assignment-container:
      SEARCH INPUT #user-search (for filtering)
      user-list-container (scrollable):
        IF @users present:
          FOR EACH user IN @users:
            LABEL with checkbox:
              check_box_tag event[assigned_user_ids][], user['id']
                CHECKED IF user id in event.assigned_user_ids
              SHOW user['name'] and user['email']
        ELSE:
          SHOW 'Loading users...'
      COUNTER: SPAN #selected-count + ' user(s) selected'

  ACTIONS:
    SUBMIT button
    LINK 'Cancel' -> events_path

  JAVASCRIPT:
    ON DOMContentLoaded:
      FUNCTION updateSelectedCount():
        count = number of checked .user-checkbox elements
        SET #selected-count text to count
      FUNCTION filterUsers():
        searchTerm = #user-search value (lowercase)
        FOR EACH checkbox:
          label = closest .user-checkbox-item
          IF userName or userEmail includes searchTerm:
            SHOW label
          ELSE:
            HIDE label
      BIND #user-search 'input' -> filterUsers
      BIND each checkbox 'change' -> updateSelectedCount
      CALL updateSelectedCount() on load

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Handles POST /events. Creates a new event with permitted params (title, description, assigned_user_ids). On success, redirects to the event's show page with a green notice. On failure, re-fetches users and re-renders the new form with errors.
implementation.name: EventsController#create
implementation.pseudo_code:
POST /events:
  @event = Event.new(event_params)
  IF @event.save:

  ELSE:

    RENDER :new with status 422

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Fetches the full list of users from the external JSONPlaceholder API (https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users). Results are cached for 5 minutes. Returns an array of user hashes with name, email, id, etc. Returns empty array on failure. This is the externally loaded user list used for assignment on event forms.
implementation.name: JsonplaceholderService.fetch_users
implementation.pseudo_code:
FUNCTION fetch_users:
  CHECK Rails cache for 'jsonplaceholder_users' (expires_in: 5 minutes):
    IF cache miss:
      uri = URI('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users')
      response = Net::HTTP.get_response(uri)
      IF response.code == '200':
        RETURN JSON.parse(response.body)
      ELSE:
        RETURN []
    ON error:
      LOG error message
      RETURN []

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Fetches a single user by ID from the external JSONPlaceholder API. Results are cached per user for 5 minutes. Used by Event#assigned_users to resolve each assigned user ID to full user data for display in event show view.
implementation.name: JsonplaceholderService.fetch_user
implementation.pseudo_code:
FUNCTION fetch_user(user_id):
  CHECK Rails cache for 'jsonplaceholder_user_{user_id}' (expires_in: 5 minutes):
    IF cache miss:
      uri = URI('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/{user_id}')
      response = Net::HTTP.get_response(uri)
      IF response.code == '200':
        RETURN JSON.parse(response.body)
      ELSE:
        RETURN nil
    ON error:
      LOG error message
      RETURN nil

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Custom getter that reads the assigned_user_ids column (stored as JSON text) and parses it into a Ruby array. Returns empty array if blank. Enables persistence of user assignments across events.
implementation.name: Event#assigned_user_ids (getter)
implementation.pseudo_code:
FUNCTION assigned_user_ids:
  value = read_attribute(:assigned_user_ids)
  IF value is blank:
    RETURN []
  RETURN JSON.parse(value)
  ON parse error:
    RETURN []

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Custom setter that serializes the assigned_user_ids array to JSON string before storing in the database text column, ensuring proper persistence.
implementation.name: Event#assigned_user_ids= (setter)
implementation.pseudo_code:
FUNCTION assigned_user_ids=(value):
  IF value is an Array:
    write_attribute(:assigned_user_ids, value.to_json)
  ELSE:
    write_attribute(:assigned_user_ids, value)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Resolves assigned user IDs to full user objects by calling JsonplaceholderService.fetch_user for each stored ID. Used in the show view to display assigned user names. Returns empty array if no IDs assigned.
implementation.name: Event#assigned_users
implementation.pseudo_code:
FUNCTION assigned_users:
  IF assigned_user_ids is blank:
    RETURN []
  FOR EACH id IN assigned_user_ids:
    CALL JsonplaceholderService.fetch_user(id)
  RETURN compact results (remove nils)
